title: An ideal contained in a principal ideal is recovered as the product with its ideal quotient
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter algebra.tex (Algebra), meta-observation about prime ideals

difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a principal ideal J and any ideal I contained in J, one has I = J (I : J) (statement lines 5332-5336). The proof does not fall back on a general theory of ideal quotients: it writes J = (a), identifies the quotient with I : a, uses that elements of I are multiples of a to get one inclusion, and uses that xJ is contained in I for x in the quotient to get the other (proof lines 5338-5344). Both inclusions have to be checked separately and the containment of I in J is what makes the first one a statement about the multiplier; the author writes both out. H2.
